details:
Project Details

Our project is an interactive educational website designed to bring the stories of inactive NASA space exploration equipment to life. It focuses on machines that once contributed to scientific discoveries on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space.

1. What does it do and how does it work?

The website allows users to explore the history and scientific contributions of different space exploration machines. We selected five missions and groups of objects, including ALSEP, Phoenix and InSight, Spirit and Opportunity, Ingenuity, and Kepler.

Each machine has its own dedicated section containing:

  • A short story: Explains its mission, discoveries, and why it became inactive, using simple and accessible language.
  • Interactive 3D model: Allows visitors to rotate and examine the machine from different angles.
  • Real NASA images: Help users connect the stories to actual space exploration missions.
  • An interactive quiz: Tests visitors' understanding of the five featured objects.

2. What are its benefits?

The project transforms complex scientific information into an accessible and engaging learning experience. Instead of reading lengthy technical reports, users can visualize the machines, interact with their 3D models, and test their knowledge. This makes learning more enjoyable, encourages curiosity, and helps visitors remember scientific information.

3. What is its intended impact?

Our main goal is to make space exploration more accessible to students and curious people. We also aim to preserve the legacy of these machines by keeping their missions, discoveries, and contributions visible. Although these machines are no longer operational, the knowledge they provided to humanity remains valuable.

4. What tools and technologies did we use?

We used:

  • OpenCode: To support the website development process.
  • Sketchfab: To integrate and present interactive 3D models.
  • NASA resources: To research the missions, collect reliable scientific information, and obtain authentic images.
  • Web technologies: To build the interactive educational experience.

5. How is the project creative?

Our creativity lies in changing the way people discover space exploration history. Rather than treating inactive machines as outdated equipment, we give each one a voice and a story. Combining storytelling, interactive 3D visualization, authentic imagery, and quizzes creates a more immersive experience that connects science with exploration.

6. What factors did our team consider?

We considered several important factors:

  • Scientific accuracy: Using NASA resources to ensure that the information is reliable and sourced.
  • Accessibility: Explaining scientific concepts in simple language for a broad audience.
  • User engagement: Combining storytelling, visual content, and interaction to maintain visitors' interest.
  • Educational value: Making sure users learn something meaningful rather than simply browsing images.
  • Historical significance: Highlighting the lasting contributions of machines that are no longer operational.

Ultimately, our guiding idea was simple: A machine may stop working, but its story and discoveries should never be forgotten.
